New: steer your agents from the notch (stop, pause, notes, plan approval), Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other agents beside Claude Code and Cursor, keyboard shortcuts, a Commands panel for what runs in the background, limit alerts, effects around the notch, and a VPN. After upgrading, open AI Notch and click Set Up once: the hooks changed.

What's new

- Stop, pause and notes: a working session's Details have Note (a line Claude gets with its next tool call, without stopping), Pause (its next tool call waits until you click Resume, at most 30 minutes) and Stop (it stops before its next tool call, as if you pressed Esc). Agents seen as processes get Pause and Stop too.
- To-do list and plans: Claude's to-do list shows on its row (done of total, and the item under way) and in Details. Edit and Write prompts show a few lines of the change. A finished plan can be approved, approved with edits accepted, or sent back to keep planning, from the notch.
- Other agents: Codex and Gemini CLI report through their own hooks: turns, tools, subagents, and a prompt waiting for you (answered in Codex or Gemini). OpenCode reports each session (terminal, `opencode serve` or the desktop app) through a plugin Set Up writes. Aider, Goose, Amp, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code and others show as processes, working or idle from their CPU. Any script or agent can show itself with `ai-notch-hook report working --agent "My Bot"`.
- Jump to the exact tab: in Terminal and iTerm2 a click on a row selects the tab the session runs in, and in tmux its window and pane. macOS asks once to let AI Notch control that app.
- Keyboard shortcuts: ⌃⌥Space opens or closes the notch, ⌃⌥J jumps to the session that needs you (else the one that finished last), and while a prompt waits ⌃⌥Y allows and ⌃⌥N denies the oldest. Setup → Effects turns them off.
- Commands panel: a terminal chip in the footer counts what runs in the background: Claude Code's background and long Bash commands and monitors, other agents' shells, and dev servers and watch builds in your terminals. Each line has its owner, time, CPU, memory, folder and ports, and Stop (a second click) ends it and everything under it. A command an agent left running after its chat ended stays listed. Setup → Machine turns it off.
- Limit alerts: a notification when Claude's 5-hour or weekly limit passes 80% and again at 95%, with when it resets and when this pace would run out. Setup → Optional turns it off.
- Prod after a push: a session that runs git push or a deploy command shows the Prod chip's state on its row for 20 minutes, red with the alerting monitor.
- Agent analytics in Datadog: Setup → Prod → Agent analytics sends Claude Code's own telemetry to Datadog. Turn Off removes it all.
- Effects: light around the closed notch while an agent works: Scanner (in the working agent's colour), Neon, Lights or Aurora, giving way to the amber glow while a session waits. A faint glow follows the pointer near the notch; Sparkles when done (off unless turned on) bursts when a turn finishes. Setup → Effects.
- A calmer look: each agent keeps one colour, its name tag; a working row has a hairline that fills against its last turn's length; new rows slide in and changes fade across. Compact rows (Setup → Effects) fits eight rows before the list scrolls.
- VPN: an OpenVPN client in the notch, with nothing else to install. A VPN chip in the footer, beside Prod and RAM: green with the profile's name while connected, amber while connecting, red after a failure, grey when off. The VPN panel has a line per profile with Connect, Disconnect or Cancel, and the address, time, traffic and log behind a chevron. A username and password, a passphrase or a one-time code is asked in a small window under the notch; a sign-in page (SSO) opens in your browser. A connection that drops shows in the collapsed notch and notifies. A connection keeps running when the notch closes or AI Notch quits.

After upgrading

- Open AI Notch and click Set Up: Pause needs a longer hook timeout, and Set Up also adds the Codex and Gemini CLI hooks and the OpenCode plugin where those are installed.
- Codex runs a hook only once you trust it: after Set Up, type /hooks in Codex and trust AI Notch's.
- OpenCode loads the plugin when it next starts.

Setting up the VPN

1. Setup → VPN → Install… asks for your admin password once. The helper copies itself, OpenVPN and OpenVPN's macOS DNS script to /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/info.ankeshshiv.notch.vpn/ and starts as a launch daemon. OpenVPN needs root for the tunnel, routes and DNS; the helper runs it only for your user.
2. Import Profile… (in Setup or the VPN panel) takes an .ovpn file from your VPN provider or admin.
3. Click the VPN chip, then Connect.

OpenVPN runs as root, so each profile is checked when imported. It is refused when it would run a program (up, down, route-up, plugin, script-security), load code (engine, providers), read or write a file by path (ca /path, auth-user-pass /path, log, status, config), or take over the helper's own settings. Certificates and keys must be inline (`<ca>…</ca>`, `<cert>`, `<key>`, `<tls-crypt>`), as exported profiles usually have them. Windows-only lines (block-outside-dns, register-dns) are left out. To check a profile first:

    /Applications/AINotch.app/Contents/Helpers/ai-notch-vpnd check ~/Downloads/work.ovpn

Known limits

- Codex: a permission prompt is answered in Codex, not in the notch. Gemini CLI: hooks need version 0.26 or later. Agents seen as processes: working or idle is a guess from CPU time, and they get no tools, titles, sounds or notifications.
- VPN: OpenVPN 2.7 only (no IKEv2, WireGuard or tap devices), one connection at a time. BF-CBC and other ciphers of OpenSSL's legacy provider are not available. If OpenVPN is killed outright (not through Disconnect), the DNS it set stays until the next connection or a network change. The helper serves the user who installed it.
- Uninstalling the app does not remove the VPN helper: click Setup → VPN → Remove first, or afterwards run `sudo /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/info.ankeshshiv.notch.vpn/ai-notch-vpnd uninstall`.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later. OpenVPN is GPLv2; its licence and where its source is are in AINotch.app/Contents/Resources/OpenVPN.
